articleTitle: Controller Selection Module for Switch Migration in Fog Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Dynamic load balancing is critical in fog computing for increasing network demands and optimizing IoT (IoT) efficiencies. This study investigates the application of the Threshold-Aware Switch Migration (TASM) method, which integrates threshold parameters into the load balancing algorithm, aiming to enhance network performance. Through a comprehensive experimental setup, the research evaluates the TASM method's effectiveness compared to traditional approaches, focusing on critical metrics such as the Load Balancing Rate (LBR) and introducing the Load Threshold Compliance Rate (LTCR). The results reveal that incorporating the threshold settings leads to a nuanced outcome. While the initial adjustment shows a slight decline in LBR, the LTCR significantly improves, indicating a more optimized load distribution across the network. These findings underscore the importance of threshold settings in fog computing, demonstrating their potential to improve network stability and efficiency. This paper contributes to the fog computing literature by showcasing how strategic adjustments in load balancing parameters can directly enhance operational dynamics and suggesting avenues for future research in dynamic and adaptive network management strategies.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of CDRA for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance enhancement of a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) for 5G wireless communication applications. The proposed CDRA is excited using a 50Ω microstrip line with an aperture slot and optimized using higher-order mode excitation and substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) techniques. The design aims to improve gain, bandwidth, and radiation efficiency while maintaining compactness and low losses. Simulation results using Ansys HFSS demonstrate significant performance improvements, achieving a peak gain of 8.2 dBi and a bandwidth of 7.68% around 28 GHz. The integration of SIW technology and some modifications, such as introducing holes in the resonator, contribute to the overall enhancement of the antenna's performance, making it suitable for high-frequency 5G applications.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Fractal Antenna Using Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper discussed the gain enhancement of the Minkowski fractal antenna with metamaterial. A conventional patched antenna is designed at 3.5 GHz as the 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>iteration and modified to the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> iteration of the Minkowski fractal antenna. The reduction of gain was observed and that is the main drawback in fractal antenna despite of its advantage in reducing the overall dimension of an antenna. Metamaterial is used in this work to enhance the gain by having a multilayer superstrate. The antenna is simulated using CST software. The performance of the antenna has been observed on the reflection coefficient and the gain through the radiation pattern. The gain of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> iteration fractal antenna with metamaterial is observed to improve from 0.96 dBi to 3.48 dBi.

articleTitle: Predictive Electromechanical Valve Monitoring System Enhanced with the Implementation of Internet of Things for Remote Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Electromechanical Valve has been used wherever it is required for fluid flow and has to be controlled automatically. They are being utilized more and more in a wide range of plants and machinery. A valve may be chosen to perfectly suit the application at hand thanks to the range of possible designs. With respect to this advancement of technology regarding electromechanical valves, this paper will portray the most recent commonly produced solutions and technologies on electromechanical valve monitoring systems to determine the conditions of the electromechanical valve that can avoid any coil failures, identify any degradation or issues with the valve and its parts and fix them before the valve fails. Electromechanical valve monitoring is crucial to ensuring that the machinery is operating as efficiently as possible. This study reviews and presents proposed experimental works of electromechanical valve monitoring systems. It is widely used in many major and high revenue industries, from agriculture to the dynamic & technology advancement automotive manufacturing, and it plays a crucial role in keeping businesses running smoothly. An effective EMV monitoring solution is intended to enable large plantation sites, real-time analysis, and the provision of online monitoring systems based on IOT deployment, especially for the strategic area at the oil and gas industry.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enabled Smart Gas Sensing Platform for Carbon Monoxide Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This study focuses on identifying the best machine learning model for carbon monoxide (CO) detection. CO, a colorless and odorless gas, poses significant health risks, making its detection crucial in various settings. The research evaluates several machine learning algorithms, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP), to enhance the precision of CO detection. The results indicate that ANN and SVM perform well but are prone to overfitting with complex data. MLP showed the highest error rate, suggesting the need for further optimization. This study highlights the importance of selecting appropriate machine learning models based on dataset characteristics and application context, aiming to improve environmental monitoring and proactive safety management.

articleTitle: Mitigating DBA Exploits: Enhanced Security Against Degradation Attacks in XG-PON
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Next-Generation Gigabit Passive Optical Networks (NG-PON) improve bandwidth and data rates, but their upstream channel security has been overlooked due to assumptions about its point-to-point nature. This paper introduces a Security-Enhanced Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation (SE-DBA) algorithm for XG-PON to address this vulnerability. SE-DBA includes a detection phase for abnormal behavior and a mitigation phase that reduces bandwidth allocation to identified attackers. Network simulations using OMNET++ demonstrate that SE-DBA improves SE-DBA increases the lawful ONU's network resilience during attacks by 50% compared to GIANT. The results also demonstrate SE-DBA's ability to penalize the malicious ONU by reducing its bandwidth request to 20% of its original request.

articleTitle: ESP Mesh Network for Security Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, the significance of data in driving operational efficiency is undeniable. Many Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are neither data ready nor have the capital to upgrade their existing machinery. This project addresses the need for a low-cost IoT ecosystem and a simplified architecture for retrofitting old machines with external sensors to enable data collection for cloud-based analysis and monitoring. The primary objectives are to establish a low-cost, reliable, and flexible solution that integrates automated connections, self-organized, and self-healing features for security applications. The developed solution involves implementing an ESP Mesh network using ESP32, ESP32-CAM, Arduino IDE, and a Telegram application. The results demonstrate the successful initialization and operation of the ESP Mesh network showcasing the nodes' ability to connect, communicate, and perform self-organizing as well as self-healing functions. The ESP-based security system outperforms similar existing systems and contributes to a low-cost IoT solution suitable for various IIoT and IoT applications.

articleTitle: High Q-Factor in 2D Photonic Crystals Structure with Different Nanocavities Formation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: In this paper, 2D photonics crystal (PhCs) structures have been simulated by varying the nanocavities parameters, specifically through shifting the position of air holes to achieve a high quality (Q)-factor. The challenge lies on optimizing the position of these position air holes to minimize the vertical scattering, which negatively impacts the Q-factor. These cavities used mode gap confinement approach in simulation to analyse how variations in the number and position of air holes affect the light confinement by measuring the Q-factor. Through these simulations, we found that by increasing the number of air holes position, will reduce the value of Q-factor due to the vertical scattering and resonance wavelength will be shifted linearly towards the highest region. However, highest value of Q-factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.07\times 10^{5}$</tex> with mode volume value of 0.64 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda/\mathrm{n})^{3}$</tex> were successfully obtained.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Circular Patch Antenna Using Tapered Feeding Line for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: In this paper a low cost Circular patch antenna with tapered feed line for 5G applications is proposed. This circular patch antenna is designed using FR-4 glass epoxy having thickness of 1.6mm this makes the antenna cost effective. The overall size of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\mathrm{X}40\mathrm{X}1.6\text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The size of the antenna is compact. This antenna is operated at the frequency of 3.5 GHz. This antenna is useful for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Sign Language Recognition System for Service-Oriented Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time sign language recognition and translation system, designed to improve communication for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community. The system uses YOLOv5 and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to translate American Sign Language (ASL) gestures into text. Trained on 2369 images and validated with 342 images covering 49 ASL signs, the model achieved high accuracy in real-time tests. Intended for service-oriented environments, this system enhances accessibility and inclusivity by facilitating communication between sign language users and those unfamiliar with ASL.

articleTitle: Comparison of Power Consumption between Tree and Ring Passive Optical Network-5G/6G Fronthaul
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation on the power consumption of fronthaul Passive Optical Networks (PONs) in the context of 5G/6G networks. The significance of this research is by addressing key aspects that influence energy efficiency in 5G/6G fronthaul, which is based on the optical transport network specifically PONs. Firstly, the parameters that significantly impact the power consumption of fronthaul PONs is identified and analyzed. Secondly, a comparative power consumption analysis between two prevalent PON topologies; namely Tree and Ring were compared. The power consumption was also compared when considering different functional split (i.e Option 6 and Option 7.2). This comparison highlights the strengths and weaknesses of each topology in terms of power consumption. Additionally, appropriate formulas for calculating the power consumption specific to PON-based 5G/6G fronthaul configurations were derived and provided. The findings offer valuable insights into power consumption performance in 5G/6G fronthaul networks, proposing that ring topology exhibits lower power consumption than tree topology and Option 6 provides up to 44% power consumption reduction for both topologies. This research contributes to the development of more sustainable and energy-efficient 5G/6G network infrastructures.

articleTitle: IoT Based Warehouse Management System Leveraging On RFID and Cloud Platform Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of logistics and supply chain management, the integration of advanced technologies has become imperative to enhance efficiency and accuracy. This paper introduces an IoT-Based Warehouse Management System that leverages Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology and Firebase Cloud platform to revolutionize inventory management in modern warehouses. By integrating these technologies, the system achieves real-time data synchronization, automated inventory tracking, and enhanced visibility, thereby addressing the limitations of traditional warehouse management systems. The implementation of this system demonstrates significant improvements in operational efficiency, inventory accuracy, and scalability, making it a robust solution for various industries. The paper also discusses the system's architecture, methodology, and preliminary results, highlighting its potential to transform warehouse operations

articleTitle: Directional Curvature and Temperature Sensor Based on Side-Polished Fiber Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: A dual-parameter sensor for directional bending and temperature sensing based on side-polished multimode fiber is proposed. In this scheme, a side-polished multimode fiber is spliced between two sections of coreless fiber to form a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The side-polished structure induces distinct phase changes when the fiber is bent from different directions. The side-polished fiber exhibits wavelength responses of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.252 \text{nm}/\mathrm{m}^{-1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-1.146 \text{nm}/\mathrm{m}^{-1}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^\circ$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$180^{\circ}$</tex> bending, respectively. This same structure is further demonstrated for high-sensitivity temperature sensing by coating it with Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The PDMS-coated sensor shows an improved sensitivity of - <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-107.9 \text{pm}/^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> compared to the uncoated sensor which attain sensitivity of 55.7 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pm}/^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. The results of this study demonstrate the sensor's potential for use in multi-parameter sensing applications, including medical wearable devices, soft robotics, and health monitoring of civil and mechanical engineering structures.

articleTitle: Mecanum-Wheeled Autonomous Mobile Robot for Flexible Manufacturing System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) are increasingly utilized across various industrial sectors, particularly in manufacturing. This study focuses on the design and implementation of an AMR equipped with four Mecanum wheels, programmed to execute diverse path planning tasks within a simulated manufacturing environment. The primary objectives are to determine the AMR's position, plan its movements, and navigate around obstacles. To achieve these goals, the AMR employs a Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithm based on the Robot Operating System (ROS), installed on a Raspberry Pi. A Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR) sensor is used for mapping. The path planning algorithm integrates the Dijkstra algorithm for global planning and the Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) for local planning, allowing the AMR to navigate autonomously based on a predefined map. User-defined target movements are executed via optimal paths determined by the AMR's navigation plan. The proposed algorithm and the AMR's navigation system were tested both in real-world path planning scenarios and in simulated environments using RViz, demonstrating their effectiveness and reliability.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence of Things Real-Time Fish Counting System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This project aims to develop a real-time fish counting system using AIoT with three main objectives: developing a fish detection model using YOLOv8 and performing both quantitative and qualitative analysis, building a GUI for the Fish Counting System, and implementing real-time counting and analysis using IoT. The YOLOv8 model achieved 90.79% precision, 94.19% recall, 85.52% average precision, and a 92.46% F1-score, with real-world accuracy at 69.97%, an average processing time of 242.05ms per frame, and a rate of 4.13 frames per second. The GUI, built with Tkinter, includes Home, History, and Graph pages, allowing users to input video via IP Camera or local drive, with historical data stored in Google Firebase. Future work includes implementing DeepSORT for better fish tracking, using a polarizing filter on the camera, expanding the dataset to include more fish species and implementation using NVIDIA TensorRT.

articleTitle: Bridging the Digital Divide: 6G Networks and Enabling Technologies for Ubiquitous Coverage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) networks are expected to support an exponential increase in connected devices and address critical concerns such as capacity, coverage, and privacy. However, one significant concern is the digital divide, which refers to the difference in accessibility, availability, and usage of communication services between urban and rural areas. The COVID-19 pandemic has emphasized the need for reliable communication services in rural areas for economic inclusion in online education, remote work, and financial services. In this paper, we examine the three levels of the digital divide: coverage, access, and usage, and analyze suitable communication technologies to mitigate coverage issues and achieve ubiquitous service. Moreover, we explore enabling technologies that can help reduce global coverage gaps. Within this context, we provide a case study involving on-demand coverage and computational services provisioning in remote rural areas to demonstrate how such measures can harness the benefits of digital farming. Finally, we conclude the paper and present future research directions.

articleTitle: Computational Analysis of No-Core Fiber Sensor for Detecting Aging Traces in Transformer Oil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The presence of aging traces in transformer oil poses a significant concern for industries heavily dependent on power transformers, as it can potentially lead to breakdowns that disrupt critical business processes. This paper introduces a computational analysis study of a no-core fiber (NCF) sensor for detecting aging traces in transformer oil. Employing the Wave Optics Module in COMSOL Multiphysics 5.5®, the computational analysis study delves into the efficacy of the no-core fiber (NCF) sensor in detecting transformer oil with refractive indices spanning from 1.46 RIU to 1.55 RIU, encompassing the typical aging range of transformer oil. The study explores various parameters, including electric field distribution, mode field diameter, and effective mode index, across a spectrum of refractive index (RI) values. The findings highlight the potential of the sensor for effectively evaluating and analyzing aging traces in transformer oil by observing the RI and electric field intensity changes. This research lays the groundwork for future applications of the sensor in real-time scenarios especially for high-RI implementation conditions, offering a promising avenue for enhancing the reliability and longevity of power transformer systems.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Optimization in HetNets for Smart Grid Wide Area Network Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The rapid expansion of smart grid infrastructure necessitates advanced communication networks capable of supporting extensive data exchange with high reliability and energy efficiency. This paper investigates energy efficiency in cellular networks using Heterogeneous Networks (HetNets) for Smart Grid Wide Area Networks (SG-WANs). HetNets, which include both macro and small cells, could enhance coverage and capacity of cellular network but are challenging to manage due to their complexity and dynamic traffic demands. This work adopts a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based framework to optimize network resources, adapting to environment changes and minimizing energy consumption while maintaining Quality of Service (QoS). The DRL agent learns to make real-time decisions on cell activation, user association, and power control, improving the network's overall energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Implementation of Real-Time Lane Detection on Autonomous Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of a learning-based lane detection algorithm on an autonomous mobile robot. More specifically, it explores the implementation of the Ultra Fast Lane Detection algorithm for real-time application on the SEATER (Single-passenger Electric Autonomous Transporter) prototype using a camera, with an emphasis on optimizing its performance on a Jetson Nano platform. Multi-core processing on the CPU and GPU has been implemented in this paper to optimize the application program and avoid delays or buffering. Preliminary experiments have been conducted to evaluate the algorithm's performance in terms of data processing speed and accuracy using two datasets: a public dataset for the outdoor environment and another dataset collected from the indoor area of the Workshop Building at BRIN Bandung. The experimental results show that after conversion to TensorRT, the algorithm achieves significantly improved performance on the Jetson Nano platform compared to the ONNX model, with processing speeds of approximately 101 ms using CULane and 105 ms using TuSimple-about 22 times faster than the previous model. While the algorithm demonstrates good accuracy on the public outdoor dataset, its performance falls short on the indoor dataset. Future work should focus on transfer learning and fine-tuning to improve indoor lane detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Role of AI and Open RAN in 6G Networks: Performance Impact and Key Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and open radio access network (RAN) into sixth-generation (6G) networks has led to significant transformation and advancement in the wireless communications industry, especially for cellular networks. It offers enhanced network performance, which is essential for future networks. This paper examines the impact of AI and O-RAN integration in the 6G architecture and possibly the latest 6G technologies, providing insight into how these technologies can benefit from the AI-based open 6G RAN architecture. We discuss the challenges of transitioning from traditional to future RAN, including interoperability, mobility, performance issues, complexity, and regulatory standards, and propose the possible future directions to these challenges.

articleTitle: Circular Virtual Array Beamforming in Wireless Sensor Network Using Backtracking Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Collaborative beamforming (CB) in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) increases the transmission distance, which allow nodes to transmit data directly can affects the sidelobe level (SLL) of the radiation beampattern, thus the energy efficiency of WSN. Therefore, a proposed AI-based algorithm is designed and implemented to optimize the radiation beampattern performance by finding the inter-element spacing between the sensor nodes based on circular antenna array. In this work, the Backtracking Search Algorithm (BSA) is adopted to implement the proposed Circular BSA. Four different cases are implemented to verify the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed algorithm to achieve the objectives of SLL suppression, adaptive main beam angle, null placement. Results show that the proposed Circular BSA overcome the previous conventional Circular Array (CFA) in all the performance metrics.

articleTitle: Semantic Communication: Implication for Resource Optimization in 6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper explores the evolution of communication systems, highlighting the transition from traditional methods to digital forms with the introduction of Semantic Communication (SemCom). We examine SemCom's role in enhancing efficiency in 6G networks by optimizing resource usage. We present a case study as a practical implication of SemCom in traffic management, specifically its use in prioritizing emergency vehicles in smart traffic systems. Additionally, we identify key areas for future research, including inference approaches, resource optimization, AI integration, and data security within SemCom. Our analysis underscores the potential of SemCom to revolutionize communication systems and its critical role in developing next-generation networks.

articleTitle: Implementation of Proposed Cryptography Algorithm on ESP32-Based IoT System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This research explores the data security of the Internet of Things (IoT), with a specific focus on designing cryptographic algorithms suitable for the resource-constrained ESP32 microcontroller. In the rapid growth of IoT, security vulnerabilities have become a concern necessitating tailored solutions to avoid generic attacks at various architectural layers. According to NIST, lightweight block ciphers especially AES-128 show their robustness under a resources-constraint environment and at the same time, ensure confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity. This project designs a lightweight block cipher cryptographic algorithm inspired by established algorithms like Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and Data Encryption Standard (DES). It leverages encryption techniques such as key generation, XOR operations, custom-designed S-boxes, custom-designed P-boxes, and row permutation methods. Understanding the structure of ESP32, the algorithm is designed to align the process data with native word size which takes advantage of optimizing the register operation. Performance analysis was conducted to balance security and execution time. The results indicate that the algorithm yields optimal randomness and demonstrates a short execution time using four rounds of encryption. Implementation on ESP32 confirms its feasibility for Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: Simple MATLAB-Based App for Markov-Switching Land Mobile Satellite Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper revisits land mobile satellite (LMS) modeling utilizing a two-state Markov chain. Detailed MATLAB code for the modeling computation is provided and explained. The LMS model in each state adheres to the Loo's distribution, with Loo's parameters extracted from the ITU-R P.681-11 report. Furthermore, the Markov-switching computation is encapsulated as a graphical user interface using MATLAB's ‘appdesigner’ feature. Leveraging both calculated and measured data from previous literature, empirical models for the steady state and transition probabilities of the Markov chain are developed.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 3D Linear and Circular Array Optimized by Imperialist Competitive Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Collaborative beamforming (CB) can enhance communication reliability and energy efficiency of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). However, careful node selection is required to reduce the peak sidelobe level (SLL) of CB to reduce interference during transmission. Prior studies have proposed mapping of array onto WSNs environment to select the appropriate nodes to perform CB. Nevertheless, the mapped arrays only perform CB in azimuth direction. The contribution of this paper is the designation of improved fitness function to suppresses peak SLL and control beamwidth size of beampattern in both azimuth and elevation directions. The proposed fitness function is used to evaluate the inter-element spacing of circular and linear arrays optimized by Imperialist Competitive Algorithm (ICA). The performance of arrays is evaluated in terms of beamwidth size, average peak SLL, stability, execution time and convergence behavior. The results show that linear array gives the best average peak SLL suppression of 67.8% compared to circular array. Besides, linear array shows consistency in suppressing peak SLL of beampattern with faster execution time and less iteration than circular array.

articleTitle: A High Performance Stacked Dielectric Resonator Antenna for 5G Mobile Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This research paper focuses on the design of the stacked dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with a wideband characteristic's antenna at 3.5 GHz. Fifth generation (5G) mobile antenna technology needs a high gain and huge bandwidth properties with 5 dB gain and 1 GHz bandwidth characteristics respectively. Therefore, a tacked DRA technique with different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> is proposed to achieve wideband. The stacked DRA is implemented with U-shape air filled along with stacked elements DRA with different dielectric properties. This technique leads to higher bandwidth and increases the gain of the antenna. The stacked DRA is simulated with HSFF software, and the analysis has been performed accordingly. The FR4 substrate with thickness of 1.6 mm and permittivity of 4.4 has been chosen in the simulation analysis. The stacked antenna has fractional bandwidth of more than 1 GHz. The performance of the antenna achieved the basis of the required bandwidth and gain which could be used in future 5G mobile applications.

articleTitle: Compact on-Metal UHF RFID Tag Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This study investigates the design and development of a compact UHF RFID tag antenna for on-metal applications. Typical UHF RFID tag antennas face limitations when placed near metallic objects, as the metal can reduce the tag's realized gain and read distance. To address this, a slotted structure is introduced in the patch design, enabling the UHF RFID tag to function efficiently even when attached to metal surfaces. The proposed tag antenna has a compact size of 48 mm by 48 mm and is mounted on a 200 mm by 200 mm metal plate. It is designed on a polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate with a thickness of 0.05 mm and a dielectric constant of 3.4. The radiating patch is connected to the ground plane via an inductive stub and operates within the UHF RFID band (860–960 MHz), resonating at 916.4 MHz. The proposed tag antenna achieves a far-read distance of approximately 5 meters. All simulation and optimization procedures were conducted using CST Microwave Studio software.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Multilayer Copper Coated Polyester Fabric at 2 GHz - 8 GHz Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper presents shielding characteristics of single as well as multilayer thin woven copper polyester fabric in the 2 GHz to 8 GHz frequency range through a free-space transmission method. Free-space characterization technique was employed to measure reflected and transmitted power scattering parameters. The measured results were incorporated into calculation of reflection and absorption losses' contribution to total shielding effectiveness (SE). SE performance for the material under test is characterized by logarithmic relation within the investigated frequency bands, where peak SE is approximately between 4 GHz until 6 GHz range. Increasing thickness by stacking multilayers of the investigated copper coated fabric was found to have minimum effects on SE. It was also observed that pure polyester textile sandwiching the copper coated fabric could improve SE. Reflection loss as opposed to absorption loss, was shown to be in declining trend from 2 GHz to 8 GHz.

articleTitle: Designing a FTTH Living Lab Facilities as Experience, Training, Assessment and Testing Center
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Good training facilities for Fiber to the Home (FTTH) are important factors in developing competence and skilled workers to cater evolving demand for FTTH infrastructure in the telecommunications industry in Malaysia. This paper presents our experience in developing FTTH living lab facilities, which are end-to-end integrated technical skills development centers that replicate actual fiber optic infrastructure in a lab environment. This FTTH living lab was used to conduct practical training on FTTH network cable installation, splicing, testing, and the configuration of triple play services. We present our experience in designing a multipurpose and cost-effective training facilities that we used as experience, training, assessment and testing center.

articleTitle: Multichannel Vessel Tracking Payload for Indonesian University Cubesat: First Result
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Vessel traffic monitoring is very important in Indonesia as it is one of the biggest archipelago countries that is in a strategic area. To increase the ship detection area, an Automatic Identification System (AIS) receiver can be installed on a low earth orbit (LEO) spacecraft, such as cubesat. In this research, a group of student has designed and tested a multichannel AIS receiver payload for cubesat. The receiver is working on AIS Class A and B simultaneously to increase the number of ships detection. This payload was designed in PC104 form factor that suitable in a regular cubesat. The on-ground testing result shows that the number of the detected vessels by this payload is more than 300% compared to an AIS single channel receiver. The furthest ship detected during the test was 38.89 km. However, some attenuators were added to mimic the propagation loss of vessels to space link. The result shows that the payload is capable of receiving the signal over 400 km.

articleTitle: Advances in Artificial Neural Network Assisted Microwave Sensors for Material Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This article reviews the current advances in planar microwave sensors assisted by artificial neural networks (ANNs) for various dielectric material characterization applications. The architecture of ANNs and intelligent sensing systems are introduced. The ability of ANNs to improve the accuracy of microwave sensors in measuring samples with multiple components and under various ambient conditions is discussed. ANNs enable the determination of complex and nonlinear relationships between sensing data and desired output data, such as complex permittivity, concentrations, and defect detection. More advanced neural network algorithms facilitate the training of more complex datasets. Finally, the current challenges and future prospects of ANN-integrated microwave sensors are discussed. It is envisaged that the summarized research efforts can provide valuable insights for scientists and engineers aiming to implement ANNs in microwave sensors.

articleTitle: The Effect of Balanced and Imbalanced Dataset on Voice Pathology Detection Using Online Sequential Extreme Learning Machine (OSELM)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Voice pathology detection is crucial for early diagnosis and treatment of vocal disorders. This research studies the effect of balanced and imbalanced datasets on the accuracy of voice pathology detection using Online Sequential Extreme Learning Machine (OSELM) on the Saarbruecken Voice Database (SVD). The dataset's balance has been identified as having a significant influence on the performance of the machine learning models. In this work, the voice signals from vowel /a/ of pathology and non-pathology classes are taken from SVD. The dataset is divided into two category which are balanced and imbalanced dataset. Then, the features of the voice signals are then extracted using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC) and fed into classifier called OSELM. The result of balanced and imbalanced dataset is assessed for its accuracy. The results showed that the model achieved an accuracy of 66.25% with the balanced dataset compared to 48% for the imbalanced dataset. These findings highlight the importance of addressing dataset balance to enhance the reliability and effectiveness of voice pathology detection systems.

articleTitle: Quantum Random Number Generation for Secure Communications Using Hybrid Hadamard Controlled-NOT Gates with XOR Bitmask
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The reliability and security of telecommunication systems depend on the quality of random number generators (RNGs). Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNGs) enhance randomness over classical methods, improving cryptographic strength. This paper evaluates three QRNG implementations using IBM quantum computers, analyzing their methodologies, performance, and limitations. We introduce a new QRNG algorithm on the IBM Quantum Experience (IBMQ) platform, using real quantum computers instead of simulators, and incorporating post-processing with XOR bit masking. Our algorithm achieves entropy 0.86458 and passes more NIST 800-90B and NIST 800–22 randomness tests, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability. This research supports secure telecommunication technologies by providing a reliable source of true randomness.

articleTitle: IoT Real Time Monitoring of a Pharma Production Environment for Product Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: In the manufacturing sector, particularly in the pharmaceutical industry, adhering to stringent quality and compliance standards has been and continues to be crucial due to the direct implications on public health and safety. Traditional methods of monitoring production processes often lack the responsiveness and precision needed to detect and rectify deviations in real time, leading to inefficiencies and potential compromises in product quality. This project proposes implementing an IoT-based system, utilizing Raspberry Pi and Node-RED programming, to enhance the accuracy, efficiency, and reliability of production processes. By providing continuous, real-time monitoring and analysis, this system aims to ensure adherence to quality standards, mitigate economic risks associated with product recalls and brand reputation, and foster a transformative shift towards more adaptive and scalable manufacturing operations.

articleTitle: IOT Based Emergency Detection and Response System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The proliferation of internet-connected devices is expanding exponentially, connecting people and devices to the Internet. This connectivity supports the Internet of Things (IoT), yet IoT safety management remains a challenge in smart cities. Issues like poor coordination among emergency teams, inadequate real-time monitoring, and lack of data-driven responses hinder efficient emergency management, causing delays, casualties, and property damage. This project introduces an efficient emergency response system (EDRS) to tackle fire hazards, gas leaks, and other emergencies. The system utilizes the Raspberry Pi 4B, integrating sensors (flame, gas, temperature, GPS) with the Blynk 2.0 IoT platform. Deep learning and the YOLO algorithm enable object detection to identify emergencies like fire and criminal actions. Results show the system accurately detects dangerous objects with an 85.4% accuracy rate and has a benefit-to-cost ratio of 11% compared to similar systems. The EDRS enhances safety and emergency management efficiency.

articleTitle: Comparison of Multiple Dielectric Resonator Antenna Shape at Millimeterwave
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The development of communication systems especially in antenna design in this era seeks to create low-cost, small-sized devices, with high gain and high bandwidth. Unfortunately, loss at millimeter-wave is very severe, especially involving microstrip antennas. To provide high gain, high bandwidth, and low loss antenna, dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) are introduced here operating at 27 GHz. The antennas are designed using HFSS with a Roger 5880 substrate with the different polygon shapes of DRA such as rectangular, hexagonal, decagonal, and octagonal. The results are then compared and the best result is hexagonal.

articleTitle: Right-Handed Circular Polarization Folded Reflectarray Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The increasing demand for higher data rates in 5G systems drives the need for efficient, high-gain antennas. This study presents the design of a Right-Handed Circular Polarization Folded Reflectarray Antenna (RHCPFRA) utilizing a multilayer Left-Handed Circular Polarization Selective Surface (LHCPSS) without vertical conductive segments, operating at 26 GHz. The design process begins with an incident LHCP wave, reflected by the LHCPSS and converted to RHCP by the reflectarray reflector, allowing the RHCP waves to pass through the LHCPSS and radiate. Simulations conducted using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software demonstrate a peak directivity of 15 dBi, broad impedance matching with return loss below -10 dB across 20–32 GHz, and an axial ratio bandwidth of 7 GHz, with a realized gain of 14.91 dB and an axial ratio of 1.2 dB at 26 GHz. These results indicate that the antenna is well-suited for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Effect of Hyperparameter Tuning to Fruit Quality Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Malaysia's agricultural sector plays a crucial role in the nation's economy and food security. One of the most pressing issues is the difficulty in identifying and addressing fruit damage early in the production cycle. Current manual inspection methods are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to human error. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a useful tool that help in automatically learning and recognizing pattern in image and to determine the quality of the fruit in agriculture industry. This project is focusing on building CNN machine learning for image classification and detection of fruit quality. The CNN model is being trained with 3 different data sets which are apple, damage apple and potato. The model is trained for two-class-set (apple, damage_apple) and three-class-set (apple, damage_apple and potato) with 1000 and 1500 images consecutively. The experimental results in this study demonstrate that the hyperparameter adjustment of machine learning algorithms has varying effects on fruit quality detection.

articleTitle: Multiclass Identification of NLOS Conditions in UWB Localization Based Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This paper explores the critical task of accurately distinguishing line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation channels in ultra-wideband (UWB) indoor localization systems. Using a comprehensive dataset of real measurements from a Qorvo DW1000 UWB device, the study evaluates the performance of multiple machine learning classifiers, including Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naive Bayes (NB), AdaBoost (ADA), Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Logistic Regression (LR), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), under various indoor conditions. The results demonstrate that machine learning techniques can effectively classify LOS, Multipath (MP), soft-NLOS, and hard-NLOS propagation channels within UWB ranging systems. XGBoost achieved the highest overall accuracy of 99.47%, followed by DT at 98.97% and RF at 98.59%. Notably, classifiers showed significant improvement with our optimized dataset, underscoring the importance of feature selection and data balancing. Even with a reduced feature set, classification accuracies remained high, validating the robustness of the models. These findings underscore the potential of machine learning to significantly enhance the precision of UWB indoor localization systems, paving the way for more reliable and accurate indoor positioning technologies.

articleTitle: Synchronizing Local Oscillator Frequencies in Beamforming Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Collaborative Beamforming (CB) which is a cooperative transmission technique where nodes act as a virtual antenna array can achieve an order of magnitude in improved signal strength, directional signal transmission, energy efficiency and node redundancy when practically deployed. However, signals arrive out of phase at the target receiver due to unsynchronized clock frequencies of local oscillators (LOs). In this article, an iterative procedure synchronizes the common message signal from multiple transmitters to the receiver. LO frequency synchronization and random phase adjustments are carried out by CB nodes at each time slot to increase the signal to noise ratio (SNR). Mean square error (MSE) of the frequency offset of the feedback signal are estimated with the developed LO estimation algorithm. This algorithm is seen to have tracked the modified Cramer-Rao lower bound (MCRLB) more closely for SNR between 7 dB and 20 dB. An improvement of 99.57% and 93.74% is recorded for LO frequency offset MSE for CB node 1 and CB node 2, respectively, when compared to another estimator. When beamforming is enabled, the percentage increase in amplitude between single and combine node with convergence achieved is 66.67%.

articleTitle: Design of Cryptography Algorithm for Data Security of a IoT System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This research explores the data security of the Internet of Things (IoT), with a specific focus on designing cryptographic algorithms suitable for the resource-constrained ESP32 microcontroller. Referencing existing Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and Data Encryption Standard (DES) algorithms, the proposed lightweight block cipher algorithm is specifically tailored for the ESP32 platform. It leverages encryption techniques such as key generation, XOR operations, custom-designed S-boxes, custom-designed P-boxes, and row permutation methods. Understanding the structure of ESP32, the algorithm is designed to align the process data with native word size which takes advantage of optimizing the register operation. Performance analysis was conducted to balance security and execution time. The results indicate that the combination of encryption techniques including key generation, XOR operation, S-box, P-box, and row permutation yields optimal randomness, with nearly 50% of bit changes in the SAC test. The design of the proposed cryptography algorithm is recommended to use four rounds of encryptions, as it passes the SAC test in the fourth round and exhibits the shortest execution time which is 3ms. Implementation on ESP32 confirms its feasibility for Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: 6G Network Slicing Vision for Post-Disaster: AI-Enabled User Prioritization and Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This study explores the potential and practical user prioritization-based network slicing solutions to mitigate communication challenges that may arise after natural disasters due to an explosive amount of data traffic requests according to the latest earthquake experience in Turkiye from the perspective of mobile network operators. Accordingly, this study investigates the development of more robust and resilient 6G communication systems by proposing the utilization of artificial intelligence/machine learning-empowered service management and orchestration applications in open radio access network intelligent controllers in both near-real time and non-real time, ensuring vital connectivity via managing service requests intelligently and assigning network slice functions in the control plane of core network accordingly during and after earthquakes.

articleTitle: Performance of Different Electromagnetic Band Gap Structures as Band Reject on Ultra-Wideband Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: This study investigates the integration of four distinct Electromagnetic Bandgap (EBG) structures within an Ultra-Wideband (UWB) planar antenna. The objective is to create a band-stop filter that suppresses unwanted frequencies in two specific bands: a lower band below 3 GHz and a higher band exceeding 5 GHz. This design allows the desired UWB signal centered around 3.5 GHz to operate without interference. The UWB antenna, fabricated on an FR-4 substrate, utilizes a half ground plane integrated with each of the four EBG configurations. These EBG structures function as filters, targeting specific frequency ranges: 2.4 GHz to 2.8 GHz and 4.5 GHz to 7.2 GHz. From the results, it can be seen that the designed EBG structures able to suppress the unwanted frequency band of the UWB antenna and allow the desired frequency band (3–4 GHz) to operate.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Deploying Smart IoT System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: In the modern world, we rely on the Internet to meet our needs for peer-to-peer services, email, and online browsing. IoT, or the Internet of Things, refers to a physical object that has an Internet protocol address and can communicate with other internet-enabled devices. Here, the most crucial thing is to instantly guarantee security between the communication devices. This paper introduces an intelligent IoT face recognition system designed and implemented using Raspberry Pi and Node-RED. The system captures face images through a camera module for face recognition. The key parts of the system include hardware connection, software installation and configuration, function implementation, and system testing and verification. Experimental results show that the system can reliably provide access control, attendance management, and smart home control functions in actual application scenarios, providing an effective solution for IoT deployment. Through this study, we show how to use existing technologies to build an intelligent IoT application, providing a reference for future research and development.

articleTitle: Luna: A Benchmark Project in the Convergence of Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things for Home Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The fast growth of technology has increased the popularity and existence of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in modern households. These devices include fans, lighting systems, door locks, and home appliances, all of which are intended to improve convenience, efficiency, and security. However, the sheer quantity of diverse devices and platforms introduces complexity, making it difficult for users to attain a genuinely integrated smart home experience. This paper investigates the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) in the building of a home automation system. The proposed system runs on a Raspberry Pi 4 and uses a Node-RED server to manage multiple IoT devices and speech-to-text (STT) functionality. This results in a centralized and streamlined experience where the user does not have to deal with multiple individual systems but can instead relay the request to the AI assistant and have it interpret the correct response to that query. The system will be compared to a benchmarked system that uses a locally executed STT algorithm. The proposed system utilized the CPU 6.78 times more than the benchmark system and responded twice as fast for appliance control and 1.66 times faster for voice output making it both faster and more power efficient.

articleTitle: Delay Optimization of Wi-Fi Mesh in Neighbourhood Area Network Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: A smart grid is an electrical network that uses digital technology to provide two-way communication between all system components, thereby managing the transmission of electricity from all generation sources to consumers. Neighbourhood Area Networks (NAN) are communication networks that enable data sharing between smart meters, sensors, and other devices. Wi-Fi can provide wireless access in homes, businesses, and public spaces, but it has a restricted range. Mesh networks can enhance the performance of Wi-Fi in terms of NAN coverage since several nodes can communicate with one another. However, mesh networks may have delays due to their spread nature, interference, and node failure. Deep Reinforcement Learning is utilized to simulate and eliminate these delays, with the goal of reducing Wi-Fi mesh delay in NAN. The significant results show a significant reduction in network delays, which improves overall network performance and reliability, thus increasing the reliability of smart grid communication within NANs.

articleTitle: Efficient Network Traffic Prediction: Harnessing Hybrid Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The prediction of network traffic plays a crucial role in Software-Defined Networking (SDN) for proactive management and dynamic traffic handling. However, obtaining accurate historical data remains a challenge in traditional networks. This study proposes a hybrid machine learning model that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (Bi-LSTM) for traffic load prediction. The model leverages both historical and real-time network traffic data to forecast future traffic dynamics. Evaluation on GEANT and Albein datasets demonstrates that the proposed model outperforms established methodologies including GRU, RNN, LSTM, and BiLSTM, with improvements in Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) ranging from 35.2% to 503% and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) ranging from 22.2% to 64%. These findings underscore the efficacy of the hybrid model in enhancing predictive accuracy within SDN frameworks, thereby offering insights for more efficient network management practices.

articleTitle: Optimal Communication Handover of SAR Drone Based on Digital Twin Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: With various potential UAV applications, the deployment of drones in groups will increase, some of which will be ad hoc. The drone group's communications network is known as the Flying Ad-hoc Network (FANET). A reliable FANET is essential to ensuring the success of any particular operation, for example, during a disaster where the existing infrastructure is not available. FANET was formed to enable communication for rescuers (human and machine, including Search and Rescue UAVs), as well as victims, in calling for help. In order to collect data more efficiently, UAVs connected to the IoT (Internet of Things) are needed, where data is automatically collected from various sensors and directly sent through the cloud or data storage systems. However, FANET has major challenges in dynamic topology caused by the high mobility of UAVs, so this dynamic results in frequent communication handovers. To overcome this challenge, it is necessary to integrate the UAV swarm network in real time with the help of digital twin technology to find out the improved handover strategy in order to improve service quality.

articleTitle: Simulation of Bare Trench Silica Fiber Sensor for Humidity Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: Trench coreless silica fiber or known as (TCSF) is a type of coreless silica fiber (CSF) which is considerably famous optical fiber for its application as humidity sensitive materials. Nevertheless, increase in cost and introducing substantial cross sensitivity of temperature due to the limitations of intrinsic and nature of foreign materials or substances complicate during the fabrication process of TCSF or CSF as based humidity sensors. Apropos, this paper introduces a simulation of a bare TCSF which the width and depth of 50μm design for humidity sensing rather than simulating a CSF to know how sensitive TCSF is. Hence, evaluation of the sensor's performance by simulating changes in the analyte refractive index, ranging from 1.000 RIU (representing air) to 1.350 RIU (representing water), to assess its humidity-sensing capabilities. These, results indicate that the bare or uncoated TCSF design successfully detects humidity (1.00 to 1.35 RI), achieving a sensitivity of 593.7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup> RIU per unit of RI change and demonstrating strong linearity with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}$</tex> value of 0.9299. Therefore, the results laid the groundwork for future optimizations of the uncoated TCSF humidity sensor's performance through suggested possible design modifications.

articleTitle: On-Body Wearable Antenna Performance Due to Different Medical Bandage Materials as the Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The paper analyses the effect of different medical bandage materials that are commercially available in the medical industry as the antennas' substrate. Simulated magnitude of the reflection coefficient |S11| have shown noticeable deviation on the return loss and the resonant frequency due to different types of flexible substrate materials. Different types of medical bandage materials are characterized in terms of permittivity and loss tangent using open-ended coaxial probe method. Results have shown notable variation of approximately 12 % on the dielectric properties values due to the body proximity. The presented work may give an insight for the development of wearable telemedicine devices specifically in telemedicine system application.

articleTitle: Anchor Placement for Enhanced Performance in Software Defined Wireless Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: In SDN, a non line-of-site situation is one in which the broadcast signal from a controller may arrive at a receiver along a path that has been penetrated, reflected, or diffracted. This results in a longer travel time and lower signal intensity for the signal traveling through the path. This work proposes a new anchor placement method in SDN that prioritizes latency and RSS under non-line-of-site. We have used the iterated weighted least squares algorithm in order to effectively limit the effects of errors on the positioning accuracy of the SDN controller and increase its performance. The results show improved inter controller latency where we have 50 non line-of-site nodes or more. Also, this research have shown the efficiency of our algorithm in maintaining the size of the cluster, minimizing network and inter anchor latency in dense environments.

articleTitle: Characterization of Traffic in the Internet of Vehicles Using Microscopic Modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
abstract: The emergence of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) as a driver for the new age of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) provides an opportunity for a wide range of services and applications driven by the various interactions that exist between a vehicle and its environment. However, the nature of road networks affects real-time vehicular movements with respect to the departure, delay, speed and arrival of vehicles. In this paper, we present a data-driven, traffic theory and microscopic traffic simulation approach that can be used in modelling the underlying vehicular network of the IoV. Using the traffic status from the A4 highway dataset in Luxembourg, we obtain vehicular volumes from the vehicle flow rate, define thresholds for traffic status using data scaling and employ microscopic modeling to create traffic scenarios. The analysis from the results of the traffic scenarios shows unique vehicular patterns due to the nature of the road network providing insights that ultimately affect the design and implementation of IoV-based services and applications.
